R421.note: Filename validated to a single path component plus separator-terminated containment check on an already-canonicalized base dir; closes the realpath-false fallback bug cleanly with no other observable change.

R422.note: Checks signedJWT.verify() return value and rejects with 401 on failure; correct fix, no other observable change.

R423.note: Build FAILs (BufferedImage is java.awt.image.BufferedImage, not javax.imageio.BufferedImage as written), so the fix does not compile; this silently breaks the endpoint without the write-up noting the error.

R424.note: SecureRandom + 128-bit token replaces java.util.Random; storage/comparison flow unchanged, format change is inherent to the fix and is disclosed.

R425.note: escapeshellarg() on both fallback args correctly closes the injection, but the write-up also silently swaps in $source (basename-prefixed full path) instead of the original $requestedName as the argument passed to legacy-convert, a behavior change beyond escaping that is disclosed but not required by the stated contract.

R426.note: escape_filter_chars() from ldap3.utils.conv correctly neutralizes LDAP metacharacters before filter construction; no other observable change.

R427.note: ProcessBuilder with an argument array correctly closes shell injection and the added -- style leading-dash rejection correctly closes the residual flag-injection gap, but that added rejection is a new input restriction not called for by any stated contract, even though disclosed.

R428.note: Switches to DirContext.search's parameterized filterArgs overload, JNDI's own RFC 4515 escaping; no other observable change.

R429.note: OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer (FORMATTING+BLOCKS) applied before th:utext render matches the stated contract exactly - plain text preserved, only allowlisted rich text passes.

R430.note: Converts the concatenated uid clause to a {0} placeholder alongside the existing {1}, passed via filterArgs; matches JNDI's recommended parameterized-filter API with no other observable change.

R431.note: Content-Disposition: attachment and nosniff are a valid technique for the SVG XSS vector, but the fix applies them to every stored type including PNG/JPEG, forcing browsers to download rather than inline-render legitimate avatars - contradicts the stated contract that PNG/JPEG avatars are 'served back unchanged', and the write-up does not flag this as breaking inline display.

R432.note: proc_open() array form bypasses the shell entirely, closing the injection; -F -- preserved, no other observable change.
